page.h1: HTS Chapter 39: Plastics and Articles Thereof — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariffs on U.S. Plastics & Plastic Articles by Market (HTS Ch. 39) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What Mexico, Canada, the EU, China, Brazil and India charge on U.S. plastic resins and articles, by market and product, with each market's chemical and food-contact rules.

intro: Tariffs are low or zero for most of the chapter's big markets: Mexico and Canada (USMCA), the EU since July 1, 2026, and Singapore charge nothing on qualifying U.S. plastics, while Japan, the UK, Brazil and India charge their MFN rates. Two things stand out: China's extra 10% duty (and a 74.9% anti-dumping duty on one resin, POM copolymer), and Canada's September 2026 surtax on a short list of consumer articles. What usually decides access instead is chemical law — whether a polymer is on the buyer's inventory — and food-contact rules, covered under each market's regulator below.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

profile.headline: Canada is the second-largest market ($14.29B, down 5.1%). Resin and most articles enter free under CUSMA, but since September 8, 2026 six tariff items — vinyl floor coverings (3918.10), narrow self-adhesive film and tape (3919.10.99), polyethylene bags (3923.21.90) and household articles (3924) — carry a 50% surtax. Headings 3918, 3919, 3923 and 3924 hold $3.31B of exports to Canada, but only the listed lines pay.

profile.headline: The EU is the third-largest market ($10.69B, up 1.5%) and polyethylene resin (3901, $2.67B) is the largest line. Until July 1, 2026 the EU charged 6.5% on most plastics; Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 now zeroes it for U.S.-origin goods, and the Commission can suspend that cut. Belgium and the Netherlands, with Antwerp and Rotterdam, take much of it.

assumptions: MFN rates are the World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) simple-average applied rates for one representative six-digit subheading per heading — the subheading with the largest 2025 U.S. exports in that heading (for example 3901.40 for polyethylene and 3926.90 for other articles) — for the most recent year WITS holds (2019–2023). National 8–10-digit lines can differ.
USMCA (Mexico, Canada) and the U.S.–Singapore FTA apply 0% to qualifying U.S.-origin goods; the normal-rate column shows each market's MFN rate for goods that do not qualify.
For the EU, Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 zeroes out Chapter 39 from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029; the normal-rate column shows the rate the EU charged before then.

China's cells add the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods to its MFN rate, and the anti-dumping duty on POM copolymer (HS 3907.1010 and 3907.1090) is shown on heading 3907 only. China's 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods, valid unless a line is covered by an exclusion until December 31, 2026, are not added because exclusions are granted line by line.

Canada's cells show the CUSMA rate and flag the headings with a line on the September 8, 2026 surtax list (SOR/2026-186, Schedule 3, 50%): only the listed tariff items pay, and the surtax has no CUSMA exemption.

India's rates are the basic customs duty only; surcharges and IGST are not included, and the February 2026 U.S.–India framework has not been implemented as far as we found. Brazil, Japan and the UK show MFN rates.
